senses.gloss: (b. h.; cmp. חָטַט, a. גָּזַל with גָּזַז)to seize, rob.
units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 1:5:13">Y. Ber. I, 3ᶜ</cite> bot. (ref. to <cite ref="I Kings 8:54">I Kings VIII, 54</cite>) <he>ככפים הללו שלא חָטְפוּ בבנין וכ׳</he> ed. Krot. (oth. ed. <he>נטפו</he>, prob. <he>נִטְנְפוּ</he>, v. <cite ref="I00581"><he>טָנַף</he></cite>) like those hands which did not rob anything at building the Temple.
<cite ref="Eichah Rabbah 1:1">Lam. R. to I, 1</cite> <he>וחֲטָפוֹ ממנה</he> and snatched it (the letter of divorce) out of her hands; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 7:26">Koh. R. to VII, 26</cite>, v. <cite ref="H00589"><he>חָטַב</he></cite>.

senses.gloss: (cmp. Lat. carpo) to do a thing with haste, esp. (v.
units: Ber. 35ᵃ sq., Tosef. ib. IV, 1) to break without benediction.

Tosef. Pes. X, 9 חוֹטְפִין מצה לתינוק matzah is distributed among the children before the regular turn in the Passover ceremonies, in order that they may not fall asleep; Pes. 109ᵃ (v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 50; oth. opin. in comment.). Part. pass. חָטוּף, f. חֲטוּפָה snatched, abrupt.

<cite ref="Moed Katan 28a">M. Kat. 28ᵃ</cite> <he>מת פתאם מיתה ח׳</he> if one dies suddenly, it is called an abrupt death (snatched by death); <cite ref="Tractate Semachot 3:9">Treat. S’maḥ. ch. III</cite> <he>לארבעה … מיתה ח׳</he> after four or five days of sickness, it is called &c.; v. <cite ref="D00432"><he>דָּחַף</he></cite>.—<he>אמן ח׳</he>, v. <cite ref="A02040"><he>אָמֵן</he> II</cite>.

senses.gloss: to be snatched, hurried. Y. Ber. VIII, end, 12ᶜ he who says ‘a hurried Amen’—יִתְחַטְּפוּ שנותיו his years will be hurried (he will die an untimely, sudden death, v. supra); Bab.
